question: Much of the rainfall along the Western Ghats is ______ as the moist air is obstructed and forced to rise along the Ghats.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Orographic__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Orographic Rainfall**

__
 
• This is also known as **Relief Rainfall**. This rainfall occurs in the regions where mountains are present along with the sea.
 
• When the moisture-filled air from the sea rises up and hits the mountain to increase longer altitude that leads to the expansion of air and lowers the temperature.
 
• Cooling down of air and condensation causes the formation of clouds.
 
• After reaching the point of saturation, rainfall happens on the sea-facing side of the mountain.
 
• The sea-facing side receives high precipitation called the **Windward Side** and the other side of the mountains receives lesser precipitation called the** Leeward Side**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

​​**Convectional Rainfall**

 
• on getting heated air becomes light and rises up in convection form.
 
• As the air expands and drops the temperature,** Cumulus Clouds** are formed.
 
• Such rain usually occurs in** the summer season**.
 
• This type of rainfall usually occurs in the Equatorial regions and the internal parts of the continents, mainly in the **Northern Hemisphere.**
 
• Such rainfall is mainly associated with **hail **and **graupel**.

**Cyclonic Rainfall**

 
• This rainfall occurs when** two different characteristics **of **air masses** comprise together.
 
• With rising water vapour they start becoming heavy and unstable, further developing convectional nuclei and forming thick clouds.
 
• Further these clouds move up and become unstable water droplets.
